candidates.name: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
support_spans: polygonal to short spindle-shaped cells formed small nests and sheets within dilated sinusoids without encapsulation
The tumor cells exhibited clear cell borders, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, hyperchromatic nuclei, frequent mitotic figures, and sparse hepatocellular necrosis
candidates.why: The presence of tumor cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, hyperchromatic nuclei, and frequent mitotic figures are characteristic of hepatocellular carcinoma.

candidates.why: The presence of tumor cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, hyperchromatic nuclei, and frequent mitotic figures suggests a malignant process, and the location within the liver is consistent with hepatocellular carcinoma.

candidates.name: Liver hemangioma

candidates.why: The presence of narrow spaces containing erythrocytes between tumor cells could suggest a vascular component, but the presence of hyperchromatic nuclei and frequent mitotic figures makes liver hemangioma less likely.
